generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

There are \(40\) observations. Since \[ \frac{3}{4}\times 40=30, \] the third quartile lies exactly between the \(30\)th and \(31\)st observations in the ordered data.

From the stem-and-leaf plot, the \(30\)th and \(31\)st observations are \[ {@final_list[30]@}\quad\text{and}\quad{@final_list[31]@}. \]

Therefore, the third quartile is \[ Q_3 = \frac{{@final_list[30]@}+{@final_list[31]@}}{2} = {@ta_disp@}. \]
